gloss: to decay; to rot; to crumble

definitions.gloss: to decay; to rot; to crumble away
definitions.explanation: For something (typically wood, buildings, or organic matter) to deteriorate over time and fall apart. Often carries a literary or evocative tone. Can also be used figuratively for reputations or names fading into obscurity.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{木|き}が{朽|く}ちていく。
examples.english: The old tree is rotting away.

examples.japanese: {廃墟|はいきょ}の{柱|はしら}はもう{朽|く}ちかけている。
examples.english: The pillars of the ruins are already beginning to crumble.

examples.japanese: {名|な}もなく{朽|く}ちていった{無数|むすう}の{兵士|へいし}たちのことを{忘|わす}れてはならない。
examples.english: We must not forget the countless soldiers who perished in obscurity.

notes: An ichidan verb with a somewhat literary or elevated register. Common collocations: {木|き}が{朽|く}ちる (wood decays), {骨|ほね}が{朽|く}ちる (bones crumble away), {名|な}が{朽|く}ちる (a name fades into obscurity). The compound {朽|く}ち{果|は}てる means 'to rot away completely.' Contrasts with the more everyday {腐|くさ}る, which focuses on biological decomposition with unpleasant qualities (smell, slime), while {朽|く}ちる suggests gradual deterioration over a long period.
